question:
A 39-year-old college student and soccer player visits her primary care physician due to knee pain that
began yesterday and has not resolved. She reports being slide tackled during a game three days ago,
with her leg struck from the outside. Swelling in the knee appeared yesterday, and she describes a
feeling of instability and lack of confidence bearing weight on the leg during athletic activities. Her
medical history is notable for asthma managed with an albuterol inhaler. Vital signs are within normal
limits, including a temperature of 98.6°F (37°C). Physical examination reveals bruising over the leg,
knee, and lateral thigh, as well as knee edema. Passive range of motion demonstrates minor clicking
and catching of the joint. Although her gait appears normal, the patient reports that the knee does not
feel stable. Further examination and imaging are performed. What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer
Choices: (A) Medial meniscal tear (B) Anterior cruciate ligament tear (C) Lateral meniscal tear (D)
Quadriceps tendon rupture (E) Tibial plateau fracture (F) Patellar subluxation (G) Patellar tendinitis (H)
Lateral collateral ligament tear (I) Medial collateral ligament tear (J) Posterior cruciate ligament tear
 A. Lateral meniscal tear

B. Patellar subluxation
C. Medial meniscal tear
D. Quadriceps tendon rupture
E. Tibial plateau fracture
F. Anterior cruciate ligament tear
G. Posterior cruciate ligament tear
H. Medial collateral ligament tear
I. Patellar tendinitis
J. Lateral collateral ligament tear
